name: Hammedatha
overview: Hammedatha is identified in Scripture as the father of Haman, the Agagite, who is portrayed as a chief adversary of the Jewish people during the reign of King Ahasuerus. The biblical narrative highlights Haman's elevated position above other princes and his hostile intentions toward the Jews, which were rooted in his lineage as the son of Hammedatha. The plot devised by Haman to destroy the Jews was ultimately reversed, and his family, including his ten sons, faced judgment for their enmity. These passages emphasize the spiritual and historical significance of Hammedatha as the progenitor of a key antagonist in the Esther account.
